title: [Epic] Memory: personal memory, extraction, compaction and consolidation
body:
Tracking issue for the memory initiative (concept folder `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/`). Goal: give every signed-in person a private, reviewable **personal memory**, fill it from chats in the background within a budget, keep long chats working through LLM compaction, and give scheduled tasks and agents a reviewed consolidation pass with "lessons" — all on the `memoryService` and storage provider iHub already runs, with governance (opt-in at platform, group, app and user level; admins see metadata only; encryption at rest; deletion cascades) shipped before capability.

## Findings in short

Based on the research in `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/research/` and the audit of today's memory code (README §4):

1. iHub already has the governance properties the research says are under-built elsewhere: scope from the principal (`server/services/memory/memoryService.js`), opt-in, owner-only content, versioned CAS writes, a budget the model can see (`<task_memory>`), a composer that never wipes. Personal memory is that design with entries instead of a markdown body.
2. No open-source memory framework fits: mem0 OSS v3 is ADD-only with MD5 dedupe and undocumented tenant isolation; Letta is a harness; Graphiti/LangMem/Cognee are Python; Honcho is AGPL. We build on the service we own (README §3, §5 Decision 1).
3. The 2026 product consensus (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) is a list of discrete, individually editable entries written by an explicit tool and by background extraction, injected as a budgeted block, with pause ≠ reset, per-chat off, sensitive categories off by default.
4. Compaction summaries and memory are separate layers; summaries never become memory records. Consolidation ("dreaming") earns its cost only for free-text notes (tasks, agents), never applied in place.
5. The hard privacy case is the run ledger, which records model-visible messages for owners **and admins**: a placeholder/redaction rule must land before the first `<user_memory>` block is ever recorded.

## Order of work

- **Phase 0 — prerequisites** (M, R1): service contract for entries, tool rename `read_memory`/`write_memory` → `memory_read`/`memory_write` (breaking, migrated), agent memory onto the provider (breaking, migrated), `activityKind: 'memory'`, `postTurn` registry, per-chat message `seq`/`revision`, ledger placeholder and redaction.
- **Phase 1 — personal memory v1** (M, R1, closes #2522): repository, handler, tools, prompt injection, routes, Settings → Memory, admin page, group permission, app section, scheduled-task `usePersonal`, deletion/retention, docs, i18n, e2e, eval set.
- **Phase 2 — extraction and review** (M, R2, closes the extraction part of #1465; #1039 closed as duplicate): extractor, budget, activity record, pending queue, import, usage line.
- **Phase 3 — LLM compaction** (M, R2/R3, closes #3192): summariser, ledger checkpoint, `/compact`, flush before drop, tasks and agents.
- **Phase 4 — consolidation and lessons** (L, R4, new issue to be opened): lessons, consolidator, sweep, proposal review, agent write approval.

## Decisions already taken

All fifteen design decisions (README §5), the ten answers of 2026-11-06 (README §8: save-then-Undo; temporary chats read but never write; per-app opt-in; `permissions.memory`; account/app/project partitions; tool rename with no alias; close #1039; users pay for extraction; encryption always on; `task.memory.usePersonal` opt-in) and the twenty ADRs in `architecture.md` §11 are binding. `architecture.md` §0 corrections C1–C12 override the README where they conflict (no `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT`; sub-agents excluded via `invokeAppInternal` context; keys `__a_`/`__p_`; pause/clear via `PATCH /api/memory-preferences` and `DELETE /api/memories?partition=`). Items marked **architect's call** there are decided; reopen them with an ADR, not in a PR.

## Child issues

**Phase 0** — P0: P0-01, P0-02, P0-03, P0-04, P0-05, P0-06, P0-07, P0-08
**Phase 1** — P1: P1-01 … P1-21
**Phase 2** — P2: P2-01 … P2-08
**Phase 3** — P3: P3-01 … P3-05
**Phase 4** — P4: P4-01 … P4-06

## Documents

- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/README.md` — research and plan (binding: §5, §6, §7, §8)
- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` — implementation architecture (binding, overrides the README per §0; §12 build order)
- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/product-plan.md` — user stories, release packaging, metrics, definition of done
- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/ux-design.md` — screens, components, i18n keys, interaction rules, accessibility
- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/engineering-plan.md` — team setup, local recipe, module guidance, tests, risks, glossary
- `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/tickets.json` — this breakdown

## Existing issues and how each is resolved

- #2522 Personal memory — implemented by Phase 1 as the concrete v1 (entries with provenance and validity, multi-function `memory` tool, `<user_memory>` block, `/settings/memory`, flag off by default, admins get no content UI); its seven open questions are answered in README §8. Closed by the Phase 1 release.
- #1039 Support a memory store — covered: ≤ 50 entries by `maxEntries`, natural-language save/update/delete by the tool, settings page, off inside agents (Decision 9). Closed as a duplicate after Phase 1 with the mapping comment (P2-US-11).
- #1465 Long-term memory + summarisation — the extraction layer is Phase 2 (debounced, budgeted, schema-validated, review queue, import); the summarisation part is Phase 3 and summaries are **not** recalled as memory (Decision 10). Embeddings/recall `k=5` are out of scope. Closed after Phase 2/3 with a comment.
- #3192 Compact long chats — Phase 3 as specified there (80 % threshold, ~40 % verbatim, cut at a user turn, ledger checkpoint on `context/compaction.summaryRef`, `/compact`, marker, tasks and agents).
- #3196 Sub-agent delegation — its rule "memory-writing tools are not available to children" is implemented by the context exclusion (C6, ADR-M09); the rest of #3196 stays open.
- #2389 / #2906 — agent memory moves onto the provider (one item of #2389, Phase 0); memory entries use the projects `KeyProvider` envelope (#2906's key provider). Both stay open for their remaining scope.

## Out of scope

Ranked retrieval and embeddings; organisation/team/shared memory; an admin content viewer; memory for agents, sub-agents, anonymous users, OAuth clients and delegated tokens; per-topic spaces; consented impersonation; a generic job queue (#1495). See product-plan §3.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M21–M26)

Accepted 2026-11-11 after a comparison with Strands Agents (`strands-amendments.md`, `research/strands_agents_memory.md`): bounded overflow read without search (M21), chat pinned to its starting entries (M22, conditional on a Phase 1 spike), extraction failure policy (M23), durable extraction catch-up (M24), validated consolidation plans (M25), read timeout (M26). Ticket bodies P0-07, P1-01, P1-06, P1-08, P1-09, P2-01, P2-02, P3-02, P4-02, P4-03, P4-04 carry the changes.

title: [Memory] Phase 0 — prerequisites and refactors (no new user capability)
body:
## Goal

Make the existing memory plumbing ready for a third scope, entries, review and consolidation without changing what scheduled tasks and agents do today (README §7 Phase 0; architecture §12 P0a–P0f plus the per-chat `seq`/`revision` of §6.8). Ships with Phase 1 as release R1 (product-plan §5.1). No feature flag: everything here is either invisible or one of the two documented breaking changes.

## Scope summary

- `memoryService` contract: `shape`, `listEntries`, `applyOperations`, `resolve(user, context)`, `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind`; `memoryPrincipal.js`.
- Tool rename `read_memory`/`write_memory` → `memory_read`/`memory_write`, clean break, migration (ADR-M17).
- Agent memory onto the provider (`agent-memory`), write cap, version-safe `memory-finalize` (ADR-M18; D4 reversed).
- `activityKind: 'memory'` end to end (ADR-M14).
- `postTurn` registry in `ChatService` (C2: nothing moves onto it yet).
- Per-chat message `seq` and `revision` counters in `ChatRepository`.
- Run-ledger placeholder and redaction (`memoryLedger.js`, ADR-M12) — an R1 ship gate that must precede the first `<user_memory>` block (P1-09).

## Children (in order)

1. P0-01 — service contract + `memoryPrincipal.js`
2. P0-02 — tool rename + migration + docs
3. P0-06 — `postTurn` registry
4. P0-08 — per-chat `seq` / `revision`
5. P0-05 — `activityKind: 'memory'`
6. P0-07 — ledger placeholder and redaction
7. P0-03 — agent memory onto the provider
8. P0-04 — version-safe `memory-finalize`

## Acceptance (product-plan §8.1, corrected by architecture §0)

- [ ] Handlers declare `shape`; `listEntries`/`applyOperations` exist; body scopes unchanged; contract tests pass.
- [ ] Agent memory in `agent-memory`; import runs once and is tested; `maxChars` enforced; finalize passes `expectedVersion` with a one-shot re-read; the two-concurrent-writes test passes.
- [ ] Rename applied everywhere in architecture §9.1; migration and fixture test pass; no alias; `builtin-app-tool-ids.json` updated.
- [ ] No `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT` (C3): the admin agent-memory route answers `VERSION_CONFLICT` as problem+json.
- [ ] `activityKind: 'memory'` in `sseV2.js`, `runReducer.js`, `toolActivity.js`, `runActivity.js`, `toolDisplay.js`; snapshot and client test pass.
- [ ] `postTurn` after `materializeAssistantTurn`; a slow or throwing handler does not delay `run/ended`.
- [ ] `isMemoryPrincipal(user)` with the `checkTaskPrincipal` exclusions and a matrix test.
- [ ] Ledger placeholder implemented and tested (expand with unchanged store, placeholder after edit/clear/deletion, no entry text in events or spill blobs).
- [ ] `docs/agents.md` storage note; `docs/releases/next/breaking-changes.md` (rename, storage move) and `fixes.md` (write cap, version-safe finalize).
- [ ] All existing scheduled-task and agent memory tests pass under the new ids.

## Risks

Moving the agent file breaks admins who edit it on disk (release note, directory renamed to `memory.imported/`); the rename breaks external callers of the old ids (documented, no alias); `postTurn` must never delay `run/ended`; three parallel migration branches must renumber on rebase (`migration-version-check.yml`).

title: [Memory] Phase 1 — personal memory v1 (#2522)
body:
## Goal

Explicit personal memory: the model saves when asked through `memory_save/update/delete/list`, the person manages a list on Settings → Memory, the `<user_memory>` block is injected within a budget, admins gate it per platform, group and app and see metadata only (README §7 Phase 1; product-plan §3 Phase 1). No extraction. Ships dark behind `features.userMemory` + `platform.memory.enabled` as release R1 together with Phase 0; closes #2522 and lets #1039 be closed as a duplicate.

## Scope summary

Config and permissions (platform schema, flag, `permissions.memory`, app `memory` section, three migrations); storage (`user-memory` namespace, sealed `UserMemoryRepository`, policy, block builder); scope (`userMemoryHandler` registered last with the fail-closed matrix); tools (`memory.json` + `userMemoryTools.js`, attach rules); prompt injection (`{{user_memory}}`, `memoryContext`, ledger wiring, `meta.extra.memory`, sub-agent exclusion); per-chat toggle; routes (`/api/memories`, `/api/memory-preferences`, admin metadata/clear); client (Settings page, chip + Undo, recalled chip, admin page, app editor section, group checkbox); scheduled-task `usePersonal` read-only; deletion cascades and retention; i18n EN+DE; `docs/memory.md`; e2e; eval set.

## Children (in order)

Day one (no Phase 0 dependency): P1-01, P1-02, P1-03, P1-04, P1-05, P1-06.
Then: P1-07 (handler) → P1-08 (tools), P1-09 (prompt), P1-10 (per-chat setting), P1-16 (scheduled `usePersonal`), P1-11 (user routes), P1-12 (admin routes), P1-17 (deletion/retention) → P1-13 (Settings page), P1-14 (chat chip and recalled chip), P1-15 (admin page) → P1-18 (i18n), P1-19 (docs and release note), P1-20 (e2e and perf), P1-21 (eval set).

## Acceptance (product-plan §8.2, corrected by architecture §0)

Every checkbox of product-plan §8.2 with: the error-code list per architecture §4.1 (no `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT`; `VERSION_CONFLICT` is reused), the group checkbox in `GroupFormEditor.jsx` (C4), seven `authorization.js` sites (C4), keys `__a_`/`__p_` (C7), pause via `PATCH /api/memory-preferences` and clear via `DELETE /api/memories?partition=` (C11). Plus README §7 Phase 1 acceptance: with the flag on a user can ask the chat app to remember a preference, see it on Settings → Memory, edit, delete, export, pause, turn memory off for a chat; admins see counts only; a deleted account leaves no `user-memory` document; the block never exceeds `promptBudgetChars`; the tool is absent for agents, scheduled runs, sub-agents and anonymous users. Dogfood exit criteria (product-plan §5.5 step 1) before R1 GA.

## Risks

Over-eager saves by capable models (tool description, `writes` approval mode, undo rate as a gate); prompt-cache churn (block after projects, date-only `updated`); a missed `authorization.js` site (matrix test); the ledger placeholder must land first (P0-07 before P1-09).

title: [Memory] Phase 2 — automatic extraction and background review (#1465)
body:
## Goal

The platform notices durable facts the person states and proposes or saves them in the background — debounced, budgeted per user per day, schema-validated, `controlsVersion`-guarded, with review optional or required and a paste-import (README §7 Phase 2; architecture §5.3, §6.4, §8.3). Ships dark behind `platform.memory.extraction.enabled` as R2; closes the extraction part of #1465; #1039 is closed as a duplicate with the mapping comment.

## Scope summary

`UserMemoryBudgetRepository`; `memoryExtractor` on the `postTurn` registry (skip rules, debounce, batch by `seq` window, prompt + JSON schema, validation, `applyOperations` with snapshot checks, telemetry hash-only, model per C12); `memoryActivity` stored summary, `_activity`, cluster-bus channels, cancel wiring on pause/clear/delete; `pending[]`, `reviewMode`, `_pending/_accept/_reject`, `_import`; `SURFACES` `'memory'` and the Usage page line; client Pending tab, review switch, import, live polling, extraction row; admin extraction settings; i18n; docs; eval gate.

## Children (in order)

P2-01 → P2-02 → P2-03 → P2-04 → P2-06; P2-05 in parallel; P2-07 and P2-08 close.

## Acceptance (product-plan §8.3)

Every checkbox of §8.3, with the pending pruning period fixed at 30 days (ux §8 Q6) and `budgetExceeded` exposed on `_activity`. README §7 Phase 2 acceptance: precision ≥ 0.8 on the 200-turn hand-labelled sample, zero sensitive-category saves without opt-in, p95 extraction latency invisible (off-turn), cost per active user per day visible on the usage page. Tests: duplicate → NOOP, contradiction → INVALIDATE + ADD, sensitive → dropped, malformed JSON → no write, daily cap → skipped, debounce, controls change → result dropped, two workers → one application, out-of-order windows, post-edit batch.

## Risks

Junk accumulation (cap, threshold, categories, review mode, the counter); model dependence on small local models (schema validation, retry, separate `extraction.modelId`); cost surprises (daily cap, usage line, off by default).

title: [Memory] Phase 3 — LLM compaction and summaries (#3192)
body:
## Goal

Long chats, scheduled runs and agent loops keep working past the context window by summarising the older part with the LLM, storing the summary as a ledger checkpoint on the existing `context/compaction` event (C8, ADR-M10) and continuing from it; `/compact` on demand; memory is flushed before turns are dropped (README §7 Phase 3; architecture §5.6). Independent of the memory flag; ships as R2 or R3; closes #3192.

## Scope summary

`summarizeIfOverBudget` with cut rules and `policies.context.summaryThresholdRatio`; checkpoint on `context/compaction.summaryRef` and prefix rebuild in `RequestBuilder`; `beforeCompaction` seam + `memoryExtractor.flushSync`; `/compact` (steer kind `compact` + `POST …/_compact`), marker, context indicator; same mechanism in `taskExecution.js` and `PromptNodeExecutor`; docs and release note; 200-turn e2e.

## Children (in order)

P3-01 → P3-02 → P3-04, P3-05; P3-03 after P2-02 (degrades to "no flush" without Phase 2).

## Acceptance (product-plan §8.4)

Every checkbox of §8.4 with C8 applied (no new ledger event). README §7 Phase 3 acceptance: a 200-turn chat on a 32k model keeps working with tokens before/after recorded; a fact stated in turn 3 and dropped at turn 150 is in memory (if durable) or in the summary (if episodic); `/compact` works on cloud and local models; a test asserts no summary text ever lands in `user-memory` except through the extractor's operations.

## Risks

Summary quality on small models (acceptance on one local model); the summary must stay volatile (test); cut-point mistakes separating a tool call from its result (cut only at a user turn or after a complete tool batch).

title: [Memory] Phase 4 — consolidation (dreaming) and lessons for tasks and agents
body:
## Goal

A nightly, reviewable pass that merges and tidies the free-text notes of busy scheduled tasks and agent profiles and proposes procedural "lessons", stored as a `proposal { baseVersion, … }` with a diff and never applied without a human unless the admin allows notes-only auto-apply (README §7 Phase 4; architecture §2.4, §5.7, §6.5, ADR-M11). Ships dark behind `platform.memory.consolidation.enabled` as R4, after R2 has produced a month of task-memory data. A GitHub issue for Phase 4 is opened before work starts (product-plan §8.5).

## Scope summary

`lessons[]` and the `sealed` envelope on body documents, `<lessons>` block, lessons routes; `memoryConsolidator` + `memoryConsolidationSweep` under `ownsClusterSingletons`; proposal routes for tasks and agent profiles with `MEMORY_PROPOSAL_STALE` / `MEMORY_PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND`; `ConsolidationProposalCard` + `NotesDiff`, `autoApply`; agent `memory.writeApproval` staging `memory_write` into `pending[]` with an admin queue; telemetry `purpose: 'memory-consolidation'`; docs; e2e three-run test.

## Children (in order)

P4-01 → P4-02 → P4-03 → P4-04; P4-05 after P4-01; P4-06 closes.

## Acceptance (product-plan §8.5, corrected by architecture §0)

Every checkbox of §8.5 with C3 applied: a stale apply answers `409 MEMORY_PROPOSAL_STALE`. README §7 Phase 4 acceptance: for a task with ≥ 5 runs the proposal is shorter than the input notes, keeps every watermark, the owner can apply or discard it; no document changes without an explicit apply (or `notes-only` auto-apply); a lesson derived from an owner correction appears in the next run's prompt.

## Risks

Token cost for busy tasks (`maxRunsRead`, nightly cadence, eligibility); wrong generalisations (review gate, provenance drop); low value for sparse tasks (eligibility threshold).

title: [Memory P0] Extend memoryService contract for entries scopes and add memoryPrincipal.js
body:
## Context

`server/services/memory/memoryService.js` registers two body-shaped scope handlers (agent `:50-87`, scheduled-task `:23, :95-98`) and resolves a scope from the principal alone (`resolveMemoryScope`, `:124-131`). Phase 1 adds an entries-shaped `user` scope that needs trusted **context** (app, chat, purpose) next to the principal. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §1.2, §3.1 (the contract), §3.2 (principal detection), §0 C1/C6; README §5 Decision 2.

## Scope

In: the contract change, `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind`, `memoryPrincipal.js`, tests. Out: the user handler itself (P1-07), any store.

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/services/memory/memoryService.js`: handlers declare `shape: 'body' | 'entries'` (default `'body'` for the two existing handlers); `resolve(user, context = {})` — pass `context` through, existing handlers ignore it; add `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind(kind, user, context = {})` (one handler, no iteration); add `listEntries(scope, filter)` and `applyOperations(scope, ops, options)` that dispatch to entries handlers and throw `NOT_SUPPORTED` on body handlers; `read`/`write` throw `NOT_SUPPORTED` on entries handlers. Update the `MemoryScopeHandler` typedef (`:39-47`).
- [ ] Keep registration order agent → scheduled-task (→ user later); `resolveMemoryScope(user)` without context behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] New `server/services/memory/memoryPrincipal.js`: `isMemoryPrincipal(user)` = not anonymous (`isAnonymousUser` / `user.id === 'anonymous'`, `server/utils/authorization.js:715, :835`), not `user.isAgent`, not `user.isOAuthClient`, `authMode` not in `DELEGATED_AUTH_MODES` (`server/services/scheduler/tasks/taskPolicy.js:34`), and `user.permissions?.memory === true`; `memoryAccessOf(user, context)` → `'readwrite' | 'read' | 'none'` (`context.chat?.temporary` → `'read'`, `context.purpose === 'scheduled-run'` → `'read'`). Copy the exclusion list of `checkTaskPrincipal` (`taskPolicy.js:137-149`) minus its permission check. Pure; no config or storage imports.
- [ ] SPDX headers; `@module` JSDoc.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given the two existing handlers, when `resolveMemoryScope(agentUser)` / `(scheduledRunUser)` run, then they return the same scopes as before and all existing memory tests pass unchanged.
- Given a handler with `shape: 'entries'`, when `listEntries`/`applyOperations` are called, then they dispatch to it; when `readMemory`/`writeMemory` are called with its scope, then `NOT_SUPPORTED` is thrown.
- Given each principal of architecture §3.2 (interactive user with/without `permissions.memory`, scheduled run, agent, OAuth client, both delegated modes, anonymous), when `isMemoryPrincipal` runs, then only the interactive user with the permission is `true`.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory-service.test.js` (extend): `shape`, dispatch, `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind`, registration order, `NOT_SUPPORTED` paths.
- `server/tests/memory/memoryPrincipal.test.js` (new): one row per exclusion, `permissions.memory` false, `memoryAccessOf` values.

## Notes

Invariants: scope from the principal (and later trusted context) only; the service knows no store and never imports routes, tools or `LLMClient` (architecture §1.3). ADR-M02. No `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT` anywhere (C3). Unblocks P0-03 and P1-07.

title: [Memory P0] Rename read_memory/write_memory to memory_read/memory_write (breaking)
body:
## Context

Decision Q6 (README §8): all memory tools form one `memory_*` family, so the agent/task tools are renamed as a **clean break with no alias** (CLAUDE.md "Breaking Changes", ADR-M17). The grep-verified target list is `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §9.1 (including C9's additions: `setupUtils.js`, the test files, and scheduled-task runtime documents under `contents/data/scheduled-tasks/`).

## Scope

In: rename shipped files and ids, every code/prompt/test/doc reference, the migration, the breaking-change note. Out: migrations `V042`, `V199`, `V202`, `V211` and their tests (frozen history), `docs/releases/5.4.0/`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Rename `server/defaults/tools/read_memory.json` → `memory_read.json`, `write_memory.json` → `memory_write.json`; rewrite `id`; reword descriptions to "your own notes for this agent profile / scheduled task" (architecture §4.5); keep `script`, `method`, `isAgentTool`, parameters.
- [ ] Ids: `server/services/tools/platformTools.js:38-49` (`PLATFORM_TOOL_FILE_IDS`) and its header comment `:8, :25`; `server/agents/runtime/agentToolRegistrar.js:42` (`MEMORY_TOOLS`); `server/services/scheduler/tasks/runMemory.js:31` (`MEMORY_TOOL_IDS`) and the protocol note `:109-134`; `server/utils/setupUtils.js:53, :60`; `server/tools/agentTools.js` comments.
- [ ] Prompt texts: `server/services/scheduler/tasks/memoryComposer.js`, `server/agents/profile/profileWorkflowSerializer.js:174-231`, `server/services/workflow/executors/PromptNodeExecutor.js` comments, `MemoryFinalizeNodeExecutor.js:15`, `server/agents/memory/memoryFile.js:159`, `client/src/features/tasks/components/TaskBadges.jsx:61` comment.
- [ ] Tests and fixtures: `server/tests/fixtures/builtin-app-tool-ids.json`, `platform-tools.test.js`, `memory-agent-compat.test.js`, `scheduled-tasks-memory-{run,tools,composer}.test.js`, `claude-style-agent-profile.test.js`, `helpers/scheduledTaskHarness.js`, `integrations/ihubConnector.test.js`, `integrations/builderRoutes.test.js`.
- [ ] Migration `V{NNN}__rename_memory_tools.js` (`create-migration` skill; self-contained): precondition any of `contents/tools/`, `contents/apps/`, `contents/agents/profiles/`, `contents/workflows/`, `contents/config/groups.json`, `contents/data/scheduled-tasks/` exists; `ctx.moveFile` `contents/tools/{read,write}_memory.json` → `memory_{read,write}.json` rewriting `id` when present; rewrite ids in apps `tools[]`, agent profiles `tools[]` and node `tools[]`, workflow node `tools[]`, groups `permissions.tools[]`, scheduled-task envelopes `data.enabledTools[]`; log every file touched; idempotent.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/agents.md`, `docs/scheduled-tasks.md`, `docs/tool-calling.md`, `docs/integrations.md`; `docs/releases/next/breaking-changes.md` entry (old/new ids table, what is migrated automatically, what external callers — MCP clients, scripts calling `/api/tools/read_memory`, admin prompt texts — must change).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given an agent profile, an app `tools[]`, a workflow node, a group grant and a scheduled-task document naming the old ids, when the migration runs, then every id reads `memory_read`/`memory_write`, `contents/tools/{read,write}_memory.json` are renamed with their `id` rewritten, and a second run changes nothing.
- Given the release, when an admin opens the changelog, then the breaking-change entry names both ids and the external-caller impact.
- `grep -rn "read_memory\|write_memory" server shared client docs` finds only the frozen migrations, their tests and `docs/releases/5.4.0/`.

## Tests

- `server/tests/migration-vNNN-rename-memory-tools.test.js` (new; `makeCtx` style of `migration-v216.test.js`): a fixture with the old ids in every location of §9.1; an admin-edited `contents/tools/read_memory.json`.
- All existing memory tests green under the new ids; `server/tests/tool-ownership.test.js` passes.

## Notes

No alias, no `Deprecation` header: the old `ALL /api/tools/read_memory` route answers 404 after the upgrade (documented). Unblocks P0-05. Number the migration at merge time (the number is assigned at merge from the highest on disk today).

title: [Memory P0] Move agent memory onto the storage provider with a write cap (breaking)
body:
## Context

Agent memory is one markdown file per profile under `contents/agents/memory/<profileId>.md` (`server/agents/memory/memoryFile.js:45-65, 107-146`) with no size cap on write (`memoryService.js:72`). Decision D4 of the task-memory concept is reversed (ADR-M18): the notes move into a provider namespace `agent-memory`, which is one item of #2389 and follows #3230's "provider mandatory" decision. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §9.2, §2.4 (fields that Phase 4 adds later), §7.5 (`maxChars`).

## Scope

In: namespace, repository, handler move, migration import, write cap, admin route conversion. Out: encryption of body documents (Phase 4, P4-01), `expectedVersion` in finalize (P0-04).

## Tasks

title: [Memory P0] Version-safe memory-finalize: pass expectedVersion, re-read once on conflict
body:
## Context

`server/services/workflow/executors/MemoryFinalizeNodeExecutor.js:17-25` drains `_pendingMemoryUpdates` and writes without `expectedVersion` — last write wins, so two concurrent runs lose one run's notes. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §9.2 (third bullet) and README §7 Phase 0.

## Scope

In: the finalize executor and the composer's `baseVersion`. Out: write approval (P4-05).

## Tasks

- [ ] `profileWorkflowSerializer.js:418-446, 671-686`: the `memory-compose` node carries the memory `version` it read as `_pendingMemoryUpdates[i].baseVersion`.
- [ ] `MemoryFinalizeNodeExecutor.js`: pass `expectedVersion: baseVersion` to the repository; on `VERSION_CONFLICT` re-read once and re-apply an `append`; a `replace` on conflict is dropped with a `noopReason: 'conflict'` step log and SSE note (never last-write-wins).
- [ ] `docs/agents.md` memory pipeline section; `docs/releases/next/fixes.md` entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given two `memory-finalize` nodes writing the same profile with the same `expectedVersion`, when both complete, then one succeeds, the other re-reads once and retries its `append`, and no write is lost.
- Given a `replace` whose base is stale, then it is dropped with the `conflict` reason and the document keeps the newer version.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memoryFinalizeNodeExecutor.test.js` (extend): concurrent appends both land; stale replace dropped; step log asserted.

## Notes

Error code is `VERSION_CONFLICT` (C3). Uses `AgentMemoryRepository` from P0-03.

title: [Memory P0] Add activityKind 'memory' to SSE contract, tool display, reducer and chat row

## Context

What a tool call was is decided on the server and sent with `tool/started` (`activityKind`, `title`, from `server/utils/toolDisplay.js`); the client and `shared/run/` never infer it from a tool id (CLAUDE.md "Run Activity", README §5 Decision 14, ADR-M14). See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §8.1, §10.2; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/ux-design.md` §3c for the row.

## Scope

In: the enum value, server labelling for the six memory tool ids, reducer/activity folding, a plain `memory` row in the client for `memory_read`/`memory_write` (Undo and entry rendering come with P1-14). Out: `meta.extra.memory` (P1-09).

## Tasks

- [ ] `sseV2.js:143`: `activityKind: z.enum(['search', 'fetch', 'tool', 'memory'])`.
- [ ] `server/utils/toolDisplay.js:42-49` `activityKindOf`: return `'memory'` for `MEMORY_TOOL_IDS = new Set(['memory_save', 'memory_update', 'memory_delete', 'memory_list', 'memory_read', 'memory_write'])` before the integration check; `toolDisplayOf` (`:72-101`) supplies the localised `title` from the tool file; no `activityScope` for memory rows.

## Tests

title: [Memory P0] Add a detached postTurn handler registry to ChatService.runTurn
body:
## Context

Phase 2's extractor needs a seam that fires after a chat turn is materialised and never delays `run/ended`. `ChatService` has no chat title generator (C2: `server/agents/runtime/titleGenerator.js:57-75` titles agent runs), so `postTurn` is new plumbing whose first and only consumer is extraction; nothing moves onto it. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §0 C2, §1.3 rule 4, §5.3.

## Scope

In: the registry module, the emit call, tests. Out: any handler (P2-02 registers the extractor from `server/startup/`).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/chat/postTurn.js`: `registerPostTurnHandler(fn)`, `unregisterPostTurnHandler(fn)`, `emitPostTurn(event)` — runs every handler in a detached promise (the `titleGenerator.js:64-75` discipline), catches and logs errors with `component: 'postTurn'`, never awaited by the caller, bounded by a per-handler timeout log (warn after 60 s, no cancellation).
- [ ] `server/services/chat/ChatService.js`: after `materializeAssistantTurn` (`:1019`, and the error path `:1046` with `outcome.status: 'error'`) call `emitPostTurn({ chatId, runId, messageId, user, app, chat, prep, outcome })`. `invokeAppInternal` (`:1507`) does **not** emit (children never extract).
- [ ] `docs/chat-persistence.md`: a paragraph on the seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a registered handler that sleeps 5 s or throws, when a turn completes, then `run/ended` is emitted at the same time as without the handler and the turn's stored result is unaffected; the error is logged once.
- Given a sub-agent child run, then no handler fires.

## Tests

- `server/tests/chat/postTurn.test.js` (new): slow handler, throwing handler, event shape, unregister; `run/ended` timing asserted with the chat-turn harness used by `server/tests/loop/chatTurn.test.js`.

## Notes

`ChatService` never names the extractor (import rule 4). Unblocks P2-02.

title: [Memory P0] Run-ledger placeholder and redaction for memory blocks and tool payloads
body:
## Context

`request/header` records the model-visible messages in full on the first call and on every change (`server/services/loop/LLMClient.js:1526`, called at `:850`; `messagesHash`, `messages`, `messagesDelta` per `runLogEvents.js:179-199`) and `GET /api/runs/:runId/events` (`server/routes/runs.js:127-161`) serves them to the owner **and to admins**. The "admins see metadata only" promise therefore needs a ledger rule before the first `<user_memory>` block is ever recorded (README §6.7; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §8.2, §5.8, §0 C5; ADR-M12). This is an R1 ship gate and must land before P1-09.

## Scope

In: `memoryLedger.js`, `LLMClient` redaction hook, `hash-only` telemetry mode, tool-definition `ledger: 'redact'`, the `redactions` contract member, replay expansion in the events route, tests. Out: the `<user_memory>` block itself (P1-06/P1-09); the owner's re-expansion needs the user handler (P1-07) — ship the expansion with a pluggable `renderBlock` resolver that P1-09 wires.

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/memory/memoryLedger.js`: `registerRedaction(preparationId, { marker, text, placeholder, refs, chars })`; `applyLedgerRedactions(messages, redactions)` replacing the exact block text with `<user_memory ref="v<version>" sha256="…" chars="…"/>` (also for `messagesDelta`); `expandRedactions(events, user, runMeta, { renderBlock })` — owner only, every ref's current version must equal `ref.version` and the rebuilt block must hash to `sha256`, else `state: 'changed'`; non-owners `state: 'redacted'`.
- [ ] `LLMClient._recordRequestHeader`: keep `messagesHash = hashPayload(messages)` over the real messages; record redacted copies; add `redactions: [{ marker, refs, chars, placeholderHash }]`. `telemetry.redaction: { messages: 'hash-only' }`: record `messagesHash`, `messageCount`, `callConfig`, no `messages`; `message/assistant` records hash and byte count only.
- [ ] Tool definitions may declare `ledger: 'redact'`: `tool/call` arguments, `tool/result` payloads and the `toolCalls` arguments inside `message/assistant` (`AgentLoop.js:621`) are recorded as `{ redacted: true, sha256, chars }` with no spill blob; the placeholder rule applies when they reappear in later `request/header` messages and deltas.
- [ ] `runLogEvents.js:179-199` `requestHeaderData` gains `redactions`; update the contract snapshot.
- [ ] `routes/runs.js:127-161`: pass events through `expandRedactions` for the JSON projection; `view=sse` (`:169-177`) never carries `request/header` and is untouched.
- [ ] Utility runs (`parentRunId`) are deleted with their parent (`RunLog.deleteRun`, `RunLog.js:796`) — verify and add a test.
- [ ] `docs/run-ledger.md`: the placeholder/redaction rule and "replay is best-effort; deletion wins".

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a prompt containing a registered block, when the ledger records `request/header`, then `messages` show the placeholder, `redactions` names marker/refs/chars, and `messagesHash` equals the hash of the real messages.
- Given the owner replays with an unchanged store, then the block is rebuilt and the hash verified; given any later change (version differs), then the viewer gets the placeholder with `state: 'changed'`; an admin always gets `state: 'redacted'`.
- Given a run that called a `ledger: 'redact'` tool, when the stored events and spill blobs are grepped for the argument text, then nothing is found.
- Given `hash-only` mode, then no `messages` are recorded.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/memoryLedger.test.js` (new): redaction in `messages` and `messagesDelta`; hash unchanged; expansion for owner/matching version; placeholder after a version change; admin never expands; `hash-only`; grep over events and blobs.
- `server/tests/loop/contracts.test.js` snapshot updated once.

## Notes

ADR-M12. There is no `server/services/loop/replay/` module (C5) — the expansion is a projection step. Until this lands, `<task_memory>` remains readable by admins through the ledger and `docs/memory.md` (P1-19) says so.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M22)

The placeholder `ref` stays the document `version`; `renderBlock(doc, { version, asOf })` takes the chat's `memoryAsOf` when the chat has one (only if ADR-M22 is confirmed by the P1-09 spike). Add a replay test with an entry created after `asOf`.

title: [Memory P0] Add per-chat message seq and revision counters to ChatRepository
body:
## Context

Background extraction (Phase 2) must order turns chronologically across edits and discard results scheduled before a truncating edit. README §6.8 specifies a per-chat message sequence number `seq` and a per-chat `revision` counter; `ChatRepository.buildMessage` (`server/services/chat/ChatRepository.js:536`) keeps its UUID `id`, and `replaceFromMessageId` (`:1705-1799`) drops history from a message and appends the regenerated turn. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §8.3 and README §6.3/§6.8 (window and watermark rules).

## Scope

In: `seq`, `nextSeq`, `revision`, backfill, tests. Out: the extraction watermark itself (P2-02 stores it on the memory document).

## Tasks

- [ ] `ChatRepository.js`: chat document gains `nextSeq` (integer, starts at 1) and `revision` (integer, starts at 0); `buildMessage` additionally takes `seq` assigned from `nextSeq` under the chat's write lock, never reused; messages that predate the field are backfilled from their array index on the first write to that chat.
- [ ] `replaceFromMessageId` increments `revision`; a read API `getChatRevision(chatId)` / expose `revision` and the last surviving `seq` on the chat document so the extractor can reset its watermark.
- [ ] `docs/chat-persistence.md`: document `seq`, `nextSeq`, `revision` and the edit semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a chat with messages written before this change, when a new message is appended, then every message has a strictly increasing `seq` and the old ones are backfilled in array order.
- Given a truncating edit that removes `seq` 3–100, then `revision` increments, the surviving messages keep their `seq`, and the regenerated turn gets a new `seq` above the previous `nextSeq`.

## Tests

- `server/tests/chat-persistence-routes.test.js` or a new `server/tests/chat/chatSeq.test.js`: backfill, monotonic `seq`, `revision` on edit, no reuse after an edit.

## Notes

Pure additive storage change; no API shape changes (the fields may appear on stored messages served by `GET` chat routes — additive per `docs/api-guidelines.md` §7). Unblocks P2-02.

title: [Memory P1] platform.memory Zod section, userMemory flag, policy settings and migration
body:
## Context

Admin controls live in `platform.memory` (README §6.6) with the exact Zod shape, bounds and defaults of `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §7.1, a `userMemory` feature flag (default off, `preview: true`) and a `V{NNN}__user_memory.js` migration (§7.4). The migration number is assigned at merge time from the highest on disk.

## Scope

In: schema, flag, `userMemoryPolicy.memorySettings` / `isUserMemoryConfigured` / `appMemoryMode` / `chatMemoryEnabled`, migration. Out: `sensitiveFilter` (P1-05), the admin page (P1-15).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/validators/platformConfigSchema.js`: `memory` section next to `scheduledTasks` (`:672`) exactly as architecture §7.1 (`enabled false`, `maxEntries 100`, `maxEntryLength 500`, `promptBudgetChars 4000`, `retentionDays 0`, `sensitiveCategories 'allowOptIn'`, `extraction { enabled false, modelId?, maxCallsPerUserPerDay 50, maxInputTokens 12000, debounceSeconds 30, messageWindowSize 6, reviewMode 'optional' }`, `consolidation { enabled false, modelId?, minRunsSinceLast 5, maxRunsRead 10, maxPriorEntryLossFraction 0.25, schedule '03:00' }`), `.passthrough().prefault({})`.
- [ ] `server/featureRegistry.js`: `{ id: 'userMemory', name: 'Personal memory', category: 'chat', default: false, preview: true }` (the `scheduledTasks` entry at `:147` is the shape); `FEATURE_IDS` feeds `app.requiredFeatures` automatically (`appConfigSchema.js:644`).
- [ ] New `server/services/memory/userMemoryPolicy.js`: `memorySettings(platform)` with clamps (`[min, max]` tables and `clampNumber` as `taskPolicy.js:70-80`; bounds 10–1000, 50–2000, 500–20000, 2000–64000, 5–600, 2–20), `isUserMemoryConfigured(features, platform)` (registration check first — `FEATURE_IDS.includes('userMemory') && isFeatureEnabled(...) && settings.enabled`, see `chatPersistence.js:94-96`), `appMemoryMode(app)`, `chatMemoryEnabled(chat)`, `effectiveReviewMode(platformMode, userMode)`.
- [ ] Migration `V{NNN}__user_memory.js`: precondition `config/platform.json` exists; `ctx.setDefault(platform, 'memory.<key>', value)` key by key so an early admin edit survives; no `features.json` change.
- [ ] `docs/memory.md` admin section stub (full doc in P1-19); `docs/configuration-migrations.md` unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a fresh or upgraded installation, when the server starts, then `userMemory` is `false`, `platform.memory.enabled` is `false`, and no memory surface is visible.
- Given out-of-range values in `platform.json`, when `memorySettings` runs, then they are clamped to the bounds.
- Given the flag registered but off, or on with `platform.memory.enabled: false`, then `isUserMemoryConfigured` is `false`; given an unregistered id, `false`.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryPolicy.test.js` (new): clamps; gating incl. unregistered flag; `appMemoryMode` for absent/`enabled:false`/`read`/`readwrite`.
- `server/tests/migration-vNNN-user-memory.test.js` (new): defaults set, existing admin values kept, idempotent.
- `tests/unit/server/default-config-schema-validation.test.js` stays green.

## Notes

Read via `configCache.getPlatform()` on every use (no restart); `npm run lint:config-access` green. Harmless with the flag off; can merge first.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M26)

Add `readTimeoutMs` to `platform.memory` (default 1500, bounds 200–10000) with the clamp in `userMemoryPolicy.memorySettings` and a migration default. Done when: the setting is in the schema export, the admin form and the migration test.

title: [Memory P1] permissions.memory in schema, authorization.js, group editor and migration
body:
## Context

Decision Q4 (README §8): a `permissions.memory` boolean like `scheduledTasks`, granted to `admins|users|authenticated` by migration, `false` for `anonymous`. C4 corrects the README: there are **seven edit sites in four functions** of `server/utils/authorization.js` plus the OAuth-client and delegated-token blocks, and the checkbox lives in `client/src/features/admin/components/GroupFormEditor.jsx:268-285`, not `AdminGroupEditPage.jsx`. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §7.3, §0 C4; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/ux-design.md` §3h.

## Scope

In: schema, every `authorization.js` site, editor checkbox, migration, matrix test. Out: using the permission (P1-07 via `isMemoryPrincipal`).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/validators/groupConfigSchema.js:34-38`: `memory: z.boolean().prefault(false)` after `projectSharing`.
- [ ] `server/utils/authorization.js`: defaults in `resolveGroupInheritance` (`:75`), parent merge (`:130-131`), own merge (`:170-171`), output (`:193`), `loadGroupPermissions` (`:298`), `getPermissionsForUser` defaults (`:416`) and merge (`:504-505`), OAuth-client block (`:792` → `memory: false`), delegated-token block (`:812` → `user.permissions.memory = false` for **both** delegated modes; a personal API key keeps project grants but never memory — architect's call).

title: [Memory P1] App schema memory section, chat-app migration and the admin app editor section
body:
## Context

See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §7.2, §2.3 (an app with `partition: 'app'` reads only its partition — architect's call, ADR-M19); `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/ux-design.md` §3e (one checkbox + two modes; `enabled: false ⇔ mode: 'off'` invariant, Q5 of ux §8).

In: schema, migration, editor section, placeholder warning. Out: scope resolution (P1-07), tool attachment (P1-08).

- [ ] `server/validators/appConfigSchema.js`: `memorySchema = z.object({ enabled, mode: off|read|readwrite, partition: account|app }).strict()` referenced from `baseAppConfigSchema` (`:536-664`) as `memory: memorySchema.optional()`; a refinement enforcing `enabled === false ⇔ mode === 'off'` (normalise on save in the admin route rather than reject, documented).

title: [Memory P1] UserMemoryRepository: sealed documents, CAS, caps, controls, applyOperations
body:
## Context

The store for personal memory: one envelope-encrypted document per (user, partition) in namespace `user-memory`, written under lock with etag compare-and-set, with every invariant of `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §2.1–§2.3, §2.5–§2.6 and the operations contract of README §6.3/§6.8 (snapshot checks, tombstones, window/watermark). Template: `server/services/scheduler/tasks/TaskMemoryRepository.js`. Encryption is always on (README §8, ADR-M16) through the projects `KeyProvider` (#2906).

## Scope

In: namespace, key/digest helper, repository with all write paths, metadata/clear for admins, `deleteOwned`, `listPartitions`, tests. Out: prompt text (P1-06), scope (P1-07), the extractor (P2-02), budget (P2-01).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/storage/namespaces.js`: `userMemory: 'user-memory'`; `docs/storage.md` table row.
- [ ] Shared `digest(value)` helper (lift `IntegrationPreferencesRepository.js:49-50` into `server/utils/` and use it from both); keys `um_<d>`, `um_<d>__a_<appId>`, `um_<d>__p_<projectId>` (C7); every key through `isValidId`; `appId` matches `APP_ID_PATTERN`, `projectId` passes `isProjectId`.
- [ ] New `server/services/memory/UserMemoryRepository.js`: envelope `ownerId = resolvePrincipal(user, { mode: platform.runLog?.identityMode || 'default' }).id` (`server/services/loop/runIdentity.js:46`, as `chatOwner.js:180`); plaintext metadata (`version`, `controlsVersion`, `enabled`, `paused`, `sensitiveOptIn`, `reviewMode`, `counts`, `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`) and a `sealed` block (`streamingAead.encrypt/decrypt/newDataKey`, `getKeyProvider(platform.projects?.encryption?.keyProvider || 'local-file').wrap/unwrap`, AAD `ihub:memory:v1|<ns>|<key>|<ownerId>`, `sha256` of the plaintext); ten-minute per-process data-key LRU evicted on `controlsVersion` change and delete.
- [ ] Write path: `locks.withLock('user-memory:<key>', fn, { ttlMs: 15000, waitMs: 5000 })`, etag CAS, first write `etag: null`, three attempts, `EtagMismatchError` → `VERSION_CONFLICT` for callers with `expectedVersion`, transparent retry otherwise; not reentrant.
- [ ] `applyOperations(scope, ops, { expectedVersion, updatedBy, sourceRef, controlsVersion, snapshotVersion, chatRevision, window, reviewMode })`: `add` / `update` / `invalidate` / `noop`; caps (`MEMORY_FULL` counting invalidated entries, `MEMORY_TOO_LONG`); neutralise text on write; normalised-text `add` → `noop` touching `updatedAt`; `invalidate` requires a successor id; `update`/`invalidate` whose `entryId` is gone or whose `updatedAt` moved → `noop`; `add` matching `recentlyDeleted[]` (7 days, max 50) → `noop`; drop the **whole** set when the document is missing (never create), `enabled: false`, `paused`, `controlsVersion` moved, `window.fromTurnId` ≠ first turn after `extraction.appliedTurns[chatId]`, or `chatRevision` stale; when `snapshotVersion` ≠ `version` return `{ dropped: 'version' }` so the caller re-extracts; park in `pending[]` with `snapshotVersion` when review is on; advance the watermark to `window.toTurnId`; `history[]` (last 20 undo records).
- [ ] `createEntry` (tools/Settings: the only creators of a document), `updateEntry` / `deleteEntry` with optional `expectedUpdatedAt` (ux §8 Q2; mismatch → `VERSION_CONFLICT`), `setControls` (bump `controlsVersion` and `version`), `clearPartition` (entries, pending, history; keep flags; bump), `listEntries(filter, { limit, cursor, includeInvalidated })`, `listPartitions(ownerIds)` (owner index), `metadata(userId)` (plaintext only, no key), `deleteOwned(ownerIds)`, `deletePartition(partition, id)` for app/project cascades.
- [ ] Errors as `MemoryError(code, message, extra)` with the codes of architecture §4.1 (`VERSION_CONFLICT`, `MEMORY_FULL`, `MEMORY_TOO_LONG`, `MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE` on storage/`KeyAccessDenied`/lock timeout/corrupt sha, `MEMORY_PAUSED`, `MEMORY_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`).
- [ ] Logging: never entry text above `debug`; log `userIdDigest`, partition, version, counts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a first write, then a document is created with `etag: null` and `version 1`; a second concurrent creator gets a conflict and retries.
- Given `maxEntries` valid+invalidated entries, when an `add` is applied, then `MEMORY_FULL`; given text over `maxEntryLength`, `MEMORY_TOO_LONG`.
- Given an entry containing `</user_memory>`, when stored, then it is neutralised.
- Given a result whose `controlsVersion` snapshot is stale, or whose window does not start at the watermark, or whose `chatRevision` is older, then the whole set is dropped and the document unchanged; given a missing document, nothing is created.
- Given a `sealed` block copied to another key or owner, then unwrap fails with `KeyAccessDenied` → `MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE`; given a corrupt `sha256`, likewise.
- Given `metadata(userId)`, then it returns counts and flags without touching a key.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryRepository.test.js` (new) covering every case of architecture §10.1 for this file, plus the multi-worker cases of README §6.8 (replayed set, two independent sets, two windows out of order, batch after an edit, tombstone match).

## Notes

ADR-M03/M04/M05/M16. `sealed` is produced and consumed only here. Security review required. Unblocks P1-07, P1-11, P1-17, P2-01.

title: [Memory P1] Sensitive-category policy and server-side never-store filter
body:
## Context

Decision 13 (README §5): sensitive categories (health, ethnicity, religion, politics, sexuality, gender identity) are off by default behind a user opt-in governed by `platform.memory.sensitiveCategories`, and some data (government IDs, criminal history, financial account numbers, immigration status, credentials) is never stored even on request — enforced in the prompt, in a server-side filter on every write path, and in the admin policy. See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §1.2 (`userMemoryPolicy.js`), §4.1 (`MEMORY_SENSITIVE_BLOCKED` details `reason: 'never' | 'optIn'`), §8.8.

## Scope

In: `sensitiveFilter`, `sensitiveCategoryPolicy`, tests. Out: the prompt wording (P1-08, P2-02), the UI card (P1-13).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/services/memory/userMemoryPolicy.js` (from P1-01): `sensitiveFilter(text)` → `{ ok: true } | { ok: false, reason: 'never', match }` for never-store shapes (IBAN with checksum, card numbers with Luhn, national-id patterns for DE/AT/CH/EU at least, API-key/token shapes, `password:`/`token:`/`secret:` prefixes, criminal-record and immigration-status keywords in EN/DE) and `{ ok: false, reason: 'optIn' }` for sensitive-category keyword lists (EN/DE) unless `allow`; `sensitiveCategoryPolicy(platform, doc)` → `{ mode: 'exclude' | 'allowOptIn' | 'allow', optedIn }`; `classifySensitive(text, flag)` combining the model's `sensitive` flag and the keyword match.
- [ ] Apply in every write path: tools (P1-08), routes (P1-11), import/extraction (P2-02, P2-04) call `assertStorable(text, { sensitive })` which throws `MEMORY_SENSITIVE_BLOCKED` with `details.reason`.
- [ ] Counts-only audit of filter rejections (`logAudit` is for admin actions — use a `warn`-free `info` log line with counts, no text) for the metric in product-plan §6.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given `sensitiveCategories: 'allowOptIn'` and `sensitiveOptIn: false`, when text matching a sensitive category is saved, then `MEMORY_SENSITIVE_BLOCKED` with `reason: 'optIn'`; given opt-in, it is stored with `sensitive: true`.
- Given never-store text (an IBAN, a card number, an API key), then `MEMORY_SENSITIVE_BLOCKED` with `reason: 'never'` regardless of opt-in or `'allow'`.
- Given a phone number, a date, a project code or a street name, then the filter passes.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryPolicy.test.js` (extend): positives and negatives in EN and DE for every pattern group; `'exclude'` hides the opt-in; `'allow'` stores without the flag.

## Notes

ADR-M13. Patterns are conservative by design (false negatives are acceptable; false positives block the user's own save and must stay rare — the negatives list is the guard).

title: [Memory P1] userMemoryBlock: budgeted block, neutralisation and ledger placeholder
body:
## Context

One pure block builder renders every read path (README §6.4; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §6.1 wording and attributes, §6.2 selection algorithm, §1.2). The block is data, not instructions, is neutralised like `<task_memory>` (`server/services/scheduler/tasks/runMemory.js:57-59 neutralizeNotes`, `:72 buildMemoryBlock`), and yields the placeholder the ledger records (P0-07).

## Scope

In: `userMemoryBlock.js` and its tests. Out: loading documents (P1-07), injection (P1-09).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/memory/userMemoryBlock.js`: `neutralizeMemoryText(text)` (tag name `user_memory`, remove `\r`, collapse newlines, escape `<` before `/?[a-z_]`); `selectEntries(partitions, budgetChars)` per §6.2 (fixed text counted first; `feedback`, `preference` first, then `profile`, `project`, `reference`; `updatedAt` desc; skip-and-continue; render account first then project in reading order); `buildUserMemoryBlock(docs, { budgetChars, access, toolsAttached, projectNames })` → `{ text, shown, entries, refs: [{ partition, key, version, sha256 }] }` or `null` for an empty valid set; attributes `entries`, `shown`, `budget`, `updated` (day precision), `access`; entry line `- [<category>] <text> (updated YYYY-MM-DD)` and `[<category>:<project name>]` for project entries; `sensitive: true` entries only when `sensitiveOptIn`; trailing paragraph names the tools only when attached, read-only wording for `access="read"`, "One entry is not shown…" only when `shown < entries`.
- [ ] `memoryPlaceholderOf(block)` → `<user_memory ref="v<version>" sha256="<sha256 of text>" chars="<n>"/>` (multi-partition: `ref` lists each partition's version, `refs` carries them) and `renderBlockForReplay(docs, refs)` used by `memoryLedger.expandRedactions`.
- [ ] Export helper `renderPromptText(docs)` (the `'prompt'` export format: the block text without attributes).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given 13 valid entries and a 4,000-char budget where one does not fit, then `shown` is 12, the two priority categories come first, a shorter later line that fits is taken, and the paragraph tells the model to call `memory_list`.
- Given an entry containing `</user_memory>` or `<task_memory>`, then the rendered block cannot be closed early and the injection-safety test passes.
- Given no valid entries, then `null` (no block; a user without memory gets a byte-identical prefix).
- Given the same documents twice on the same day, then the text and `sha256` are identical.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryBlock.test.js` (new): snapshot; budget cases; neutralisation; `access="read"` wording; placeholder hash stability; project labelling; sensitive gating.

## Notes

ADR-M06. Pure functions only; also imported by `routes/runs.js` for replay. Unblocks P1-07, P1-09.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M21, ADR-M22)

The trailing paragraph names the unshown entries per category when `shown < entries` ("2 entries are not shown (profile 1, reference 1); call memory_list with a category to see them"); §6.2 returns `unshownByCategory`. Reserve an optional `asOf` parameter on `buildUserMemoryBlock` (entries with `createdAt <= asOf`; `entries`/`shown` are as-of values) and snapshot-test it. Done when: the snapshot covers overflow with two categories and an `asOf` case.

title: [Memory P1] userMemoryHandler: user scope from principal plus trusted context, fail closed
body:
## Context

The third scope `{ kind: 'user' }` is resolved from the trusted principal plus server-assembled context and registered **last** (README §5 Decision 2, Decision 9; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §3.1 context shape, §3.2 resolution matrix and the eight fail-closed rules, §2.3 partition table, §0 C6 for sub-agents, ADR-M02/M09/M19).

## Scope

In: the handler, registration, `readForPrompt` through the block builder, matrix tests. Out: callers (P1-08, P1-09, P1-11, P1-16).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/memory/userMemoryHandler.js`: `kind: 'user'`, `shape: 'entries'`; `resolve(user, context)` implements rules 1–8 of §3.2 as ordered `return null`s: `!isMemoryPrincipal(user)`; `!isUserMemoryConfigured(features, platform)`; `context.runKind === 'subagent' | 'agent'` or `user.scheduledRun` without `purpose: 'scheduled-run'`; `purpose` `chat`/`tool` without `context.app` or `appMemoryMode(app) === 'off'`; app partition only with `app.memory.partition === 'app'`, project partition only when `context.projectId` equals the chat's container project and `permissionsFor(project, user)` (`server/middleware/projectAccess.js:113`) grants read; `context.chat?.settings?.memory === false` → null, `context.chat?.temporary` → `access: 'read'`; document `enabled: false` or `paused: true` → null (flags read once per resolve and cached on `context`); `purpose: 'scheduled-run'` requires `task.memory.usePersonal` and gives `access: 'read'`, account only. Missing `context.purpose` → null (the body tools can never reach personal memory).
- [ ] Return `{ kind: 'user', userId, ownerId, partitions: [{ partition: 'account', key }, { partition: 'project' | 'app', key, projectId? | appId? }], access, appId, chatId, controlsVersion }`; an app with `partition: 'app'` returns only its app partition (ADR-M19).
- [ ] `readForPrompt(scope, { budgetChars })` loads the partition documents (fail-open on storage/key errors: return `{ block: null, reason: 'unavailable' }` and `warn`) and calls `buildUserMemoryBlock`; `listEntries` / `applyOperations` delegate to the repository; `read` / `write` throw `NOT_SUPPORTED`.
- [ ] Register with `registerMemoryScopeHandler` at the end of the file; `memoryService.js` imports the module last so the order is agent → scheduled-task → user.

## Acceptance criteria

- The table of architecture §3.2 holds cell by cell: only an interactive user with `permissions.memory` resolves (RW / R as the context says); a scheduled run resolves only for `purpose: 'scheduled-run'` with `usePersonal`, read-only, account partition; agents, sub-agents, OAuth clients, delegated tokens and anonymous never resolve.
- Given a chat bound to a project, then `partitions` is account + that project, never another; given an app with `partition: 'app'`, only the app partition.
- Given `paused` or `enabled: false`, then null for every context (pause stops reading and writing).

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryHandler.test.js` (new): table-driven 8 principals × 8 contexts plus one row per fail-closed rule; partition resolution with a bound project and a revoked membership; `access` values; flag off; registration order.

## Notes

`appId`/`projectId` come only from `context` (never a tool argument or query string). Security review required. Unblocks P1-08, P1-09, P1-11, P1-16, P2-02.

title: [Memory P1] memory tool file, userMemoryTools.js and attach rules in getToolsForApp
body:
## Context

The hot write path (README §6.3): one shipped multi-function file expanded into `memory_save`, `memory_update`, `memory_delete`, `memory_list`, identity from `params.user` only, recoverable failures returned as `{ error: true, code }`, `sideEffect: 'write'` so tool-approval `writes` mode applies. Contracts: `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §4.5 (schemas, results, description policy), §5.1 (sequence), §8.8; ADR-M07.

## Scope

In: tool file, implementation, ownership, attach rules, display title, tests. Out: the chip (P1-14), extraction (P2).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/defaults/tools/memory.json` in the format of `knowledge.json`: `id: 'memory'`, localised `name`/`description` EN/DE carrying the save policy (durable facts, stable preferences, standing decisions, corrections; never credentials/keys/account numbers/other people's identifiers; never tool or fetched content; never anything derivable from the chat or the app's instructions; prefer `memory_update`/`replaces`; "forget" → `memory_delete`; the sensitive rule), `script: 'userMemoryTools.js'`, `functions: { save, update, delete, list }` with the parameter schemas of §4.5 (`text`, `category`, `scope`, `replaces`, `sensitive`; `id`; `category`, `includeInvalidated`, `limit`); `sideEffect: 'write'` on save/update/delete, `'read'` on list; `dataFlow: 'internal'`; `ledger: 'redact'` (P0-07).
- [ ] `server/services/tools/platformTools.js:38-49`: add `'memory'` to `PLATFORM_TOOL_FILE_IDS` (and the header comment); `server/tests/tool-ownership.test.js` passes.
- [ ] New `server/tools/userMemoryTools.js`: `memorySave`, `memoryUpdate`, `memoryDelete`, `memoryList`; scope via `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind('user', params.user, { purpose: 'tool', app: params.appConfig, chatId: params.chatId, chat })`; ignore any `userId`/`appId`/`projectId`/`partition` argument; write in a read context → `{ error: true, code: 'MEMORY_READ_ONLY' }`; `assertStorable` (P1-05); default write target = project partition when bound unless `scope: 'account'`; `replaces` → `invalidate` + `add`; results exactly as §4.5 (`entry`, `before`, `id`, `partitions`, `budget`; never a `userId` or key); `sourceRef { chatId, runId, messageId }`, `source: 'tool'`, `confidence: 1`, `updatedBy: 'tool:<chatId>'`.
- [ ] `server/services/tools/appTools.js:129 getToolsForApp`: attach all four when `appMemoryMode(app) === 'readwrite'`, the chat is persistent, the per-chat setting is on and the scope resolves; only `memory_list` for `mode: 'read'` or a temporary/ephemeral chat; none otherwise (needs `context.chat` / `memoryScope` from `RequestBuilder`, P1-09 — land the attach call with the flag off first).
- [ ] `server/utils/toolDisplay.js`: titles "Save memory" / "Update memory" / "Remove memory" / "Look up memory" (EN/DE from the tool file).
- [ ] Add the memory guidance line to the system prompt only when the tools are attached (the block's trailing paragraph from P1-06 covers it; no second prompt).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a readwrite app and a persistent chat, when the user says "remember that I write customer emails in formal German", then the model calls `memory_save`, the entry is stored with `source: 'tool'`, `confidence: 1`, `sourceRef.chatId`, and `tool/started` carries `activityKind: 'memory'`.
- Given `mode: 'read'` or a temporary chat, then only `memory_list` is in the tool list and a `memory_save` call (direct route) answers `{ error: true, code: 'MEMORY_READ_ONLY' }`.
- Given `maxEntries` entries, then `memory_save` returns `{ error: true, code: 'MEMORY_FULL' }` (no throw); over-length → `MEMORY_TOO_LONG`; sensitive without opt-in → `MEMORY_SENSITIVE_BLOCKED`; paused → `MEMORY_PAUSED`.
- Given tool approval in `writes` mode, then `memory_save` pauses for approval and `memory_list` never does.
- Given `scope: 'account'` in a project chat, then the entry lands in the account partition.

## Tests

- `server/tests/tools/userMemoryTools.test.js` (new): scope from `params.user` only (a `userId`/`partition` argument is ignored); every `{ error, code }` return; `replaces`; `scope: 'account'`; read-only context; results carry no key or user id.
- `server/tests/platform-tools.test.js`, `tool-ownership.test.js` updated.

## Notes

Security review required. ADR-M07/M09. The direct tool route already applies `withTrustedToolContext` (`server/routes/toolRoutes.js:173`); #2522's prerequisite is met.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M21)

`memory_list` serialises at most `2 × promptBudgetChars` characters in the selection order of §6.2 and returns `truncated: true` when entries were cut. No free-text `query` parameter (decided 2026-11-11: no keyword or ranked search in memory yet). Done when: a 100-entry document of maximum-length entries yields a capped result with `truncated`, and `category` narrows it below the cap.

title: [Memory P1] Inject <user_memory> in PromptService: ledger, meta frame, no sub-agents
body:
## Context

Prompt assembly happens in exactly one function, `PromptService.processMessageTemplates` (`server/services/PromptService.js:374`), in the order app system → variables → temporal → projects (`_applyProjects`, `:190`, applied `:526`) → skills (`:548`) → style → output format. The block goes after projects and before skills, honouring `{{user_memory}}` as `{{projects}}` is honoured (`:191-192`), with the ledger placeholder registered for every recorded prompt (P0-07). See `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.2, §6.3, §8.1 (`meta.extra.memory`), §0 C6 (sub-agents) and C10.

## Scope

In: injection, `memoryContext` in `RequestBuilder`, `ledgerRedactions` → `telemetry.redactions`, the `meta` frame, `invokeAppInternal` exclusion, tool attachment wiring, replay `renderBlock` wiring, integration tests. Out: scheduled runs (P1-16).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/services/chat/RequestBuilder.js:370 prepareChatRequest`: build `memoryContext = { purpose: 'chat', app, chatId, chat: { temporary, settings }, projectId }` next to `chatContext` (`:634-642`), resolve the scope once (`resolveMemoryScopeOfKind('user', user, memoryContext)`), pass it into `processMessageTemplates` (`:654`) and into `getToolsForApp` (P1-08), and put `prep.memoryScope` and `prep.ledgerRedactions` on the prep.
- [ ] `PromptService.processMessageTemplates`: after `_applyProjects` and before skills, `readForPrompt(scope, { budgetChars })`; replace `{{user_memory}}` when present (empty string when nothing to inject), else append; unknown placeholders stay intact; `bypassAppPrompts` skips memory; register the redaction with `memoryLedger.registerRedaction` and return `ledgerRedactions` next to `llmMessages`.
- [ ] `server/services/chat/ChatService.js:467 runTurn`: pass `telemetry.redactions` into `agentLoop.run`; emit a `meta` frame with `extra.memory = { recalled, shown, access }` (or `{ recalled: 0, reason: 'unavailable' }`) right after `run/started`; `runActivity.buildRunActivity` keeps it in the stored activity; `client/src/features/chat/runToMessage.js:171 addToolSideChannels` projects it to `message.memory` (client part in P1-14).
- [ ] `ChatService.invokeAppInternal` (`:1507`): pass `memory: 'off'` / `runKind: 'subagent'` into `prepareChatRequest` so the child resolves no scope and gets no tools.
- [ ] Wire `memoryLedger.expandRedactions` in `routes/runs.js` with `renderBlock` from the user handler (owner replay).
- [ ] `docs/sse-v2.md` `meta.extra` table row `memory`; `docs/chat-persistence.md` prompt order note.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given valid entries, when a chat in an app with `memory.mode !== 'off'` starts, then the system prompt contains the `<user_memory entries= shown= budget= updated= access=>` block between projects and skills (or at the placeholder), the `meta` frame carries `extra.memory`, and the recorded `request/header` shows the placeholder.
- Given a temporary chat, then the block is injected with `access="read"` and only `memory_list` is attached; given "Memory off" in chat settings, then no block and no tools; given a user without entries or with the flag off, then the system prompt is byte-identical to today.
- Given `invokeAppInternal`, then the child has no block and no memory tools although the parent does.
- Given an entry containing `</user_memory>`, then it cannot close the block.

## Tests

- `tests/integration/memory-prompt.test.js` (new): with and without placeholder; position; `bypassAppPrompts`; injection safety; two partitions in one budget; `access="read"`; byte-identical prefix.
- `tests/integration/memory-subagent.test.js` (new).
- `server/tests/loop/chatTurn.test.js` (extend): `meta.extra.memory` frame and `telemetry.redactions` reach `LLMClient`.

## Notes

ADR-M06/M09/M12/M14. Security review required (prompt injection, ledger). P0-07 must have landed: the first `<user_memory>` block ever recorded is a placeholder.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M26, ADR-M22 (spike))

(1) The prompt-path read is bounded by `platform.memory.readTimeoutMs`: on expiry no block, `meta.extra.memory.reason: 'timeout'`, a `warn` log, the turn proceeds; add the perf-test case. (2) **Spike first**: read `server/adapters/anthropic.js`, `bedrock.js`, `openai-responses.js` and `promptCaching.js` and write down where the cache breakpoint sits relative to the system prompt and the messages; record cached-token counts per chat on memory-enabled turns if the usage normaliser exposes them. Outcome in the PR description: ADR-M22 confirmed (the `memoryAsOf` implementation then lands no later than P2-02) or withdrawn (revert `architecture.md` §6.3 and README Decision 17).

title: [Memory P1] Per-chat 'Memory off' setting and the actions-menu toggle
body:
## Context

A per-chat "Memory off" toggle stored in the chat `settings` like `enabledTools` (`server/services/chat/ChatRepository.js:306-313 CHAT_SETTING_TYPES`), honoured before the first turn and sticky thereafter (README §6.5; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §3.2 architect's call on the toggle; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/ux-design.md` §3c "Per-chat 'Memory for this chat' toggle" and the temporary-chat static line).

## Scope

In: the setting, the menu row, the temporary-chat note, tests. Out: the resolution rule itself (P1-07 reads `chat.settings.memory`).

## Tasks

- [ ] `ChatRepository.js`: `memory: 'boolean'` in `CHAT_SETTING_TYPES`; default on (absent = on).
- [ ] `client/src/features/chat/components/ChatInputActionsMenu.jsx`: new section **Memory** between "Message context" and the integration picker as a `menuitemcheckbox` row with `SwitchIndicator` (`:7, :28-35`); rendered only when the app's `memory.mode !== 'off'`, the user has `permissions.memory` and memory is enabled and not paused; paused → `aria-disabled` with `chat.memory.pausedHelp` and a link; off → the trigger's dot indicator (`offCount` pattern); after the first turn the description says `chat.memory.offSince`; temporary chat → static line `chat.memory.temporaryNote` with `eye-slash`. Persist with the chat settings through `useAppSettings.js`.
- [ ] i18n `chat.memory.*` EN/DE (ux §4.7).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a new chat, when the user sets "Memory off" before the first message, then `settings.memory === false` is stored, no block is injected, no `memory_*` tool is attached, and the state is visible in the popover; changed mid-chat, it applies from the next turn.

- `server/tests/chat-persistence-routes.test.js` (extend): the setting round-trips and rejects a non-boolean.

The server decides (P1-07 reads the stored flag); the client only renders.

title: [Memory P1] User routes /api/memories and /api/memory-preferences, partitions, export
body:
## Context

The HTTP contract of `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §4.2 (table) and §4.1 (codes), per `docs/api-guidelines.md`: plural nouns, `_action` only for transitions, `201` + `Location` + `ETag`, `204` on delete, `ServiceError` with registry codes, `{ items, nextCursor }`; pause/resume as `PATCH /api/memory-preferences { paused }`, clear as `DELETE /api/memories?partition=` (C11). The partition selector is untrusted input on a direct request and fails closed.

## Scope

In: `routes/memories.js`, error codes, limiter, OpenAPI comments, route tests. Out: `_activity`, `_pending`, `_import` (P2-03/P2-04), admin routes (P1-12).

## Tasks

No `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT`.
- [ ] New `server/routes/memories.js` (`authRequired`; register where `routes/scheduledTasks.js` is registered): the shared partition helper (load the app via `configCache.getApps()` + `isAppAllowed` + `app.memory.partition === 'app'`; the project via `ProjectService` + `permissionsFor`; failure → `MEMORY_PARTITION_NOT_FOUND`, never a fallback); `GET /api/memories` (`limit` default 50 max 200, opaque `cursor`, `category`, `includeInvalidated`, response with `partition` meta); `POST /api/memories` (`201`, `Location: /api/memories/{id}?partition=…`, `ETag`, `source: 'user'`, `restoreOf` for the chip's delete-undo per ux §5.1); `PATCH /api/memories/{id}` (merge patch, `If-Match` or `expectedUpdatedAt` → `VERSION_CONFLICT`); `DELETE /api/memories/{id}` (`?expectedUpdatedAt=`); `DELETE /api/memories?partition=` (`204`, bumps `controlsVersion`); `GET /api/memories/_partitions` (account first, always listed; app/project names resolved; inaccessible partitions omitted); `POST /api/memories/_export` (`format: 'json' | 'prompt'`, `Cache-Control: no-store`); `GET /api/memory-preferences` (creates nothing; `limits`, `counts`, `effectiveReviewMode`) and `PATCH /api/memory-preferences` (`enabled`, `paused`, `sensitiveOptIn`, `reviewMode`; `enabled`/`paused` bump `controlsVersion` on all partitions; switching `sensitiveOptIn` off removes sensitive entries, ux §3a).
- [ ] Principal gate: not a memory principal → `MEMORY_DISABLED` (anonymous → `AUTH_REQUIRED` from `authRequired`); scope via `resolveMemoryScopeOfKind('user', req.user, { purpose: 'settings', partition, appId, projectId })`.
- [ ] `memoryLimiter` copied from `routes/scheduledTasks.js:94-103` (60 writes / 15 min, `userKey` `:73`) on every mutating endpoint.

- [ ] Run the `api-design` and `api-security` skills before review.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given each endpoint, when exercised, then status, body shape, `problem+json` with `code` on errors, `Location`/`ETag` on `201`, `204` on delete and `{ items, nextCursor }` paging match §4.2.
- Given an unknown or unauthorised `appId`/`projectId`, then `404 MEMORY_PARTITION_NOT_FOUND` and nothing is read from the account store.
- Given a user without `permissions.memory`, an OAuth client or a delegated token, then `403 MEMORY_DISABLED`.
- Given `PATCH { paused: true }`, then `controlsVersion` increments on every partition of the user; `{ enabled: false }` likewise; neither deletes.
- Given 61 writes in 15 minutes, then `429` with `Retry-After`.

## Tests

body:
## Context

README §6.7: a `userMemory` step in `USER_CLEANUP_STEPS` deleting under both owner ids, a retention sweep, a `docs/pii-data-handling.md` row, no entry text in logs. `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.4 (ordering: after `chats`, before `userPrompts`; cancels timers; publishes the controls event; erases utility-run ledgers), §1.2 (`memoryRetention.js`, singleton worker only), §2.3 (app `onAppDeleted` → `deletePartition`; `ProjectService.onDeleted` hook, `server/services/projects/ProjectService.js:149, :415`), §8.3.

## Scope

In: deletion step, cascades, retention sweep, PII doc, log rule check. Out: extraction-timer cancellation implementation (P2-03 provides `cancelExtractionsFor`; call it through a no-op hook now).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/services/userDeletion.js:74-240`: step `{ name: 'userMemory', kind: 'content' }` after `chats` and before `userPrompts`: `deleteOwned(await ownerIdsOf(userId))` (`:53`), delete the budget document, call the extraction-cancel hook, publish `user-memory:controls`, delete runs with `purpose ∈ { user-memory, memory-consolidation, memory-import }` under the user's principal ids through the run index; idempotent.
- [ ] Project deletion: register an `onDeleted` hook that calls `deletePartition('project', projectId)` for every user (owner-index scan of keys ending `__p_<projectId>`); app deletion in the admin apps route: `deletePartition('app', appId)`.
- [ ] New `server/services/memory/memoryRetention.js`: `startMemoryRetentionSweep()` / `stop…` on the `chatRetention.js:448-519` pattern (daily, `unref()`, never throw out of `tick`); expire entries with `updatedAt` older than `retentionDays` (0 keeps valid entries), invalidated entries older than 180 days, `pending` older than 30 days; delete documents of users absent that long; counts-only audit summary; started in `server/startup/worker.js:249-305` under `ownsClusterSingletons`.
- [ ] `docs/pii-data-handling.md` summary row ("Personal memory entries", default off, `contents/data/user-memory/` envelope-encrypted, referenced by hash in the run ledger, switches).
- [ ] Grep-based test that no log line above `debug` in the memory modules includes `entry.text`/`text` fields (or a logger wrapper that strips them).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a user with an account store and app/project partitions, when the `userMemory` step runs, then no `user-memory` or `user-memory-budget` document remains under either owner id, and a second run finds nothing.
- Given `retentionDays > 0`, when the sweep runs, then older entries are removed and absent users' documents deleted; given `0`, valid entries stay.
- Given a deleted project or app, then its partition is gone for every user.

## Tests

- `server/tests/userDeletion-memory.test.js` (new or extend the existing deletion test): both owner ids; idempotence; budget document.
- `server/tests/memory/memoryRetention.test.js` (new): expiry rules; `retentionDays: 0`; absent-user deletion.
- Project/app cascade tests in the respective suites.

## Notes

ADR-M05 (retention prunes invalidated history), ADR-M16. Sweeps run on one worker only.
