title: [Memory P2] UserMemoryBudgetRepository: per-user daily extraction slots with CAS
body:
## Context

Users pay for their own extraction (README §5 Decision 15) and a per-user daily cap stops runaway cost: a cluster-wide budget document reserved **before** the LLM call and released only when the failure proves no request reached the provider (README §7 Phase 2; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §2.2, §8.3 "Rate limiter per worker").

## Scope

In: namespace, repository, tests. Out: calling it (P2-02), `_import` (P2-04).

## Tasks

- [ ] `server/storage/namespaces.js`: `userMemoryBudget: 'user-memory-budget'`; `docs/storage.md` row.
- [ ] New `server/services/memory/UserMemoryBudgetRepository.js`: key `umb_<d>` (shared digest helper), owner = the user, no encryption; `reserveExtractionSlot(userId, { cap })` under `locks.withLock('user-memory-budget:<key>')`: day rollover (`day !== today` → `{ day, calls: 0, skipped: 0 }`), `cap > 0 && calls >= cap` → `{ ok: false }` and `skipped += 1` (`cap === 0` is unlimited: the counter still advances, `{ ok: false }` is never returned), else `calls += 1` with CAS and `{ ok: true, release() }`; `release()` decrements once and is called only when the failure proves no request reached the provider (read failure before the call, local quota pre-check, connection-level error); timeouts, 5xx and unclassified outcomes keep the slot (architecture §2.2); `cap: 0` = unlimited; `status(userId)` → `{ day, calls, skipped, cap }` for `GET /api/memory-preferences` and `_activity.budgetExceeded`; deleted by the `userMemory` cleanup step (P1-17 hook).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given 50 reservations on one day with cap 50, then the 51st returns `{ ok: false }` and `skipped` is 1; given cap 0, then the 51st returns `{ ok: true }` and `calls` is 51; given a new day, the counter resets; given `release()` called twice, the counter decrements once.
- Given two workers reserving concurrently, then CAS serialises them and the count is exact.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryBudgetRepository.test.js` (new): day rollover; cap; cap 0 unlimited; release once; concurrent reservations with an injected `EtagMismatchError`.

## Notes

ADR-M08/M15. One document per user whatever the partition.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M23, ADR-M24)

The budget document gains the `extraction` object of `architecture.md` §2.2.1: `chats` (watermarkSeq, failures, window), `consecutiveFailures`, `pausedUntil`, `due` (at most 20, with `attempts`). Repository methods: `recordFailure(userId, chatId, class, watermarkSeq)`, `recordSuccess`, `addDue`, `removeDue`, `breakerState`. Measure the listing cost of the catch-up sweep with 10 000 documents and record the result. Done when: unit tests cover the poison-batch counters, the breaker window and the bounded `due` list under CAS contention.

title: [Memory P2] memoryExtractor: debounced, budgeted, schema-validated extraction on postTurn
body:
## Context

The background write path (README §5 Decision 8, §6.3, §6.8, §6.11; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.3 sequence, §6.4 prompt and JSON schema, §8.3 multi-worker, §8.4 telemetry, §8.6 error handling, §0 C12 model choice; ADR-M08). Registered on the `postTurn` registry from `server/startup/` so `ChatService` never names it.

## Scope

In: the extractor module, prompt, schema, validation, apply with snapshot checks, telemetry, registration. Out: the stored activity record (P2-03), pending UI (P2-06), budget repository (P2-01).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/memory/memoryExtractor.js`: `onPostTurn(event)` skip rules (not `isMemoryPrincipal`, `extraction.enabled` false, `appMemoryMode !== 'readwrite'`, temporary chat, `chat.settings.memory === false`, paused/disabled, fewer than two user turns, `outcome.status !== 'completed'`, scope null); per-worker debounce map (`MAX_PENDING_EXTRACTIONS = 1000`, oldest cancelled; cancel-and-reschedule per chat; `debounceSeconds` default 30; durable `due` entry and catch-up sweep instead of a chat-close trigger, see the amendment below); snapshot `{ controlsVersion, version, chatRevision, watermark }` at schedule time.
- [ ] Run: `reserveExtractionSlot(userId, { cap })` → no slot → log, stop (no reschedule); the call is `llmClient.complete({ …, retries: 0 })` so one reservation is one transport attempt (`LLMClient` would otherwise retry transient failures internally and report only the last error); batch = next `messageWindowSize` stored turns with `seq > watermark` in `seq` order (gaps skipped), shortened **from the end** to `maxInputTokens` (`estimateTokens`, `shared/tokenEstimator.js`), tool results and attachments replaced by `[tool result omitted]`; `window: { fromTurnId, toTurnId }`; messages = system prompt of §6.4 (with `{sensitiveRule}` and `{maxEntryLength}`), user message with `<existing_entries>`, `<conversation_summary>` (Phase 3) and `<recent_turns>`; `llmClient.complete({ model, messages, options: { responseFormat: 'json', responseSchema }, timeoutMs: 60000, telemetry: { kind: 'utility', purpose: 'user-memory', user, parentRunId: runId, surface: 'memory', refs: { chatId }, redaction: { messages: 'hash-only' } } })`; model = `platform.memory.extraction.modelId` or the turn's `prep.model.id` (C12).
- [ ] Validate: `extractJson` → `createOutputValidator(schema)` (`server/services/inference/structuredOutput.js:444`), one retry with `jsonInstruction` (`:410`) that reserves its own slot first (no slot → `failed`, no write, no reschedule), then `failed`; post-schema: `entryId` exists, `evidenceTurn` offered, bare `invalidate` dropped, `confidence ≥ 0.7`, sensitive policy and `sensitiveFilter`, dedupe; `applyOperations(scope, ops, { controlsVersion, snapshotVersion, chatRevision, window, sourceRef: { chatId, runId, messageId }, updatedBy: 'extraction:<chatId>', reviewMode: effective })`; `{ dropped: 'version' }` → re-extract the same window once against the current document (counted against the cap); backlog → reschedule immediately.
- [ ] Failure handling per §8.6 and §2.2: `readPlain` failure before the call (`KeyAccessDenied`, `MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE`), local quota pre-check or connection-level error (refused, DNS) → `release()`; timeout/5xx/unclassified → slot kept (the request may have been billed); `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` → skipped, counted on the budget document, logged at `info`; malformed after retry → no write.
- [ ] `cancelExtractionsFor(userId)` (local timers) and a `clusterBus.subscribe('user-memory:controls', …)` that cancels remote timers; `flushSync({ user, chatId, runId, turns, timeoutMs })` for Phase 3 (one bounded call, errors swallowed).
- [ ] Register from `server/startup/worker.js` (or `server/startup/services`) with `registerPostTurnHandler`; configReloadHooks need no entry (per-use config read).
- [ ] Call `recordMemoryActivity` (P2-03) with `{ added, updated, invalidated, pending }`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a persistent chat with ≥ 2 user turns in a readwrite app with extraction on, when a turn completes, then one `complete` runs after the debounce over the window and the current entries, operations with confidence ≥ 0.7 are applied under lock with CAS, added entries carry `source: 'extraction'`, `confidence`, `sourceRef.messageId`.
- Given a duplicate fact → `noop`; a contradiction → `invalidate` + `add`; a sensitive proposal without opt-in → dropped; malformed JSON twice → no write; a bare `invalidate` → dropped; an unknown `evidenceTurn` → dropped.
- Given a temporary chat, "Memory off", `mode: 'read'`, a paused user or < 2 user turns, then no LLM call is made (asserted on the fake).
- Given the daily cap reached, then the call is skipped and not rescheduled; given one slot left and malformed output, then the retry is not made and nothing is written; given a provider connection error on a `retries: 0` call, the slot is released; given a timeout, it is kept.
- Given a pause/clear/delete between schedule and apply, then the whole result is dropped and no document is created; given two workers applying the same set, one write; given two results with distinct windows finishing out of order, the stale one is dropped and the next batch rescheduled; given a result scheduled before a truncating edit, it is discarded.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/memoryExtractor.test.js` (new) with `new LLMClient({ transport })` fakes: every case above, the debounce (cancel-and-reschedule; durable `due` entry and catch-up sweep, ADR-M24), telemetry fields incl. `hash-only`, model choice per C12, the backlog loop, `flushSync` bounded to one call.

## Notes

Never creates a document. Only user and assistant text is extracted from (MINJA mitigation, §8.8). Security review required. Unblocks P2-03, P3-03.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M22, ADR-M23, ADR-M24)

Replace "immediate on chat close" (there is no such event): add the chat to `due` on first debounce, remove it on finish, skip or cancel, and run `startMemoryExtractionCatchupSweep()` every 5 minutes under `ownsClusterSingletons`; graceful shutdown flushes pending chats once with a 5 s cap. Failure policy as in `architecture.md` §2.2.1: content-class vs availability-class, window halving after two failures at the same watermark, a visible skip of a one-turn batch (`activity.memory.skipped`), the per-user breaker (5 failures, 1 h). Apply `asOf` through the block builder if the P1-09 spike confirmed ADR-M22. Tests are listed in `architecture.md` §10.8. Done when: the poison-turn, outage, breaker and restart tests pass.

title: [Memory P2] Review queue (pending, accept, reject), reviewMode and paste-import endpoint
body:
## Context

Hermes-style pending approval: with review on, every extraction `add`/`update` is parked in `pending[]` with its `snapshotVersion` and the person accepts or rejects (README §6.3; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §2.1 pending shape, §4.2 `_pending`/`_accept`/`_reject`/`_import` rows, §5.3 `reviewMode` precedence `required > on > off`, §0 C11 — the pending family stays `_action` because accept/reject are transitions).

## Scope

In: repository pending operations, routes, `reviewMode` on preferences, import over the same contract. Out: UI (P2-06).

## Tasks

- [ ] `UserMemoryRepository`: `listPending`, `acceptPending(id, { text? })` under the lock — re-validate per operation when `snapshotVersion !== version` (`update`/`invalidate` downgraded to `noop` when the entry is gone or moved; `add` applied only after the UI confirmed "your memory changed since this was proposed", carried as `confirmChanged: true`), the accepted entry is `source: 'user'`, `confidence: 1`; `rejectPending(id)`; `pendingRetentionDays = 30` constant (pruned by P1-17's sweep); `counts.pending`.
- [ ] `server/routes/memories.js`: `GET /api/memories/_pending?partition…` → `{ items, nextCursor }`; `POST /api/memories/_pending/{id}/_accept` `{ text?, confirmChanged? }` → `200` entry (409 `VERSION_CONFLICT` with `details.changed: true` when confirmation is needed); `POST …/_reject` → `204`; `PATCH /api/memory-preferences { reviewMode }` honouring `platform.memory.extraction.reviewMode` (`required` → cannot switch off; `off` → not settable); `GET` returns `effectiveReviewMode`.
- [ ] `POST /api/memories/_import` `{ text }` (≤ 20,000 chars) or `{ entries: [{ text, category? }] }`: reserve a budget slot (429 `MEMORY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` to midnight UTC), run the extractor's operations contract with `purpose: 'memory-import'`, `source: 'import'`, confidence 1, dedupe, sensitive filtering; `200 { items, skipped: [{ text, reason }] }`.
- [ ] `memoryLimiter` on the mutating endpoints; OpenAPI; `api-design` skill.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given `reviewMode: 'optional'` and the user's switch on, then extraction results go to `pending[]`; Accept creates the entry, Reject discards; given `'required'`, every user is in review and cannot switch off; given `'off'`, the setting is hidden and not settable.
- Given a proposal whose `snapshotVersion` differs, then accept of an `add` needs `confirmChanged`; an `update` of a vanished entry becomes `noop`.
- Given pasted text, then entries carry `source: 'import'`, duplicates are `noop`, sensitive filtering applies, and a cap hit answers `429`.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/userMemoryRepository.test.js` (extend): pending accept/reject incl. stale snapshot paths; pruning age.
- `server/tests/routes/memories.test.js` (extend): the four endpoints, `reviewMode` precedence, import incl. 429.

## Notes

Pending items count against `maxEntries` only when accepted. `invalidate` is never parked.

title: [Memory P3] summarizeIfOverBudget: threshold, cut rules, summary prompt and model config
body:
## Context

Today `server/services/loop/contextCompaction.js` does micro-compaction only (`microcompactMessages` `:22`, `compactIfOversized` `:54`, `isContextOverflowError` `:80`), applied by `AgentLoop` proactively and once reactively on overflow (`AgentLoop.js:551-570`). #3192 asks for a real LLM summary triggered by reported `promptTokens` against `model.contextWindow` (README §7 Phase 3; `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.6; ADR-M10).

## Scope

In: the planner and summariser, config, the loop trigger. Out: ledger checkpoint and prefix rebuild (P3-02), `/compact` (P3-04), flush (P3-03).

## Tasks

- [ ] `contextCompaction.js`: `planSummaryCompaction({ messages, model, previousSummary, usage, policy })` → `{ dropRange, keepFrom }` or null — trigger when reported `promptTokens` (`normalizeUsage`, fallback estimate) ≥ `policies.context.summaryThresholdRatio` (default 0.8) × `model.contextWindow`; keep the most recent ~40 % verbatim; cut only at a user turn or after a complete tool batch; keep `ask_user` answers and approvals verbatim; `summarizeIfOverBudget({ messages, model, previousSummary, llmClient, telemetry })` → strips base64 and tool outputs > 2,000 chars, prompt = previous summary + dropped turns, `llmClient.complete` with the summary model (`policies.context.summaryModelId` or the run model), returns `{ summary, dropped, usageBefore, usageAfter }`; the rebuilt context = `[system, a user message carrying <conversation_summary>, an assistant "Understood.", …kept]`.
- [ ] `server/validators/platformConfigSchema.js`: `policies.context.summaryThresholdRatio` (0.5–0.95, default 0.8), `summaryModelId?`; admin settings exposure (a field on an existing admin page or `AdminMemoryPage`'s context section — architect's call: the LLM timeouts/policies page).
- [ ] `AgentLoop.js`: after each step evaluate the plan; run the summariser before the next model call; the overflow path (`:551-570`) still compacts once.
- [ ] `docs/agent-loop.md`: threshold, model, cut rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given reported `promptTokens` above the threshold, when the next step is prepared, then the older part is summarised with the previous summary as input, ~40 % stays verbatim, the cut lands at a user turn or after a complete tool batch, base64 and large tool outputs are stripped, `ask_user` answers and approvals stay verbatim.
- Given a context-overflow error, then the loop still compacts once and retries.

## Tests

- `server/tests/loop/chatCompaction.test.js` (extend) and `server/tests/loop/summaryCompaction.test.js` (new) with fakes: threshold, cut points incl. a tool batch, kept items, stripped content, overflow path.

## Notes

The summary is derived state: never written to `user-memory` (test in P3-03). Unblocks P3-02, P3-03.

title: [Memory P3] Ledger checkpoint on context/compaction.summaryRef and prefix rebuild
body:
## Context

The ledger already declares `context/compaction` with `summaryRef` (`shared/runEvents.js:62`; `server/services/loop/contracts/runLogEvents.js:417-423`) and `AgentLoop` runs the `onCompaction` seam (`AgentLoop.js:570`), so the summary is stored on that event as a spill blob — no new event type (C8). Later turns start from the newest checkpoint (`concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.6).

## Tasks

- [ ] `AgentLoop`: on a summary compaction record `context/compaction { step, trigger: 'summary' | 'manual', collapsed, freedChars, shadowedRange: [from, to], summaryRef (spill blob), summaryHash, model, tokensBefore, tokensAfter }`; call `runHooks(seams, 'onCompaction', …)`.
- [ ] `server/services/chat/RequestBuilder.js`: when building the next turn, read the last `context/compaction` of the chat's runs (through `RunLog`), rebuild the prefix `[system, <conversation_summary>, "Understood.", turns after shadowedRange]`, and expose `prep.conversationSummary` for the extractor (P2-02 `<conversation_summary>`) and the scheduled-task composer's user message.
- [ ] `routes/runs.js` events projection: `summaryRef` is readable by the owner (the summary is chat content, not memory; admins see it as they see the transcript).
- [ ] `docs/run-ledger.md`, `docs/chat-persistence.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a compaction, then the ledger event records which turns, which model and tokens before/after, and `summaryRef` resolves to the summary text; given a later turn, then its prompt starts from the newest checkpoint and the full transcript remains stored and visible.

## Tests

- `server/tests/loop/checkpointResume.test.js` (extend) or `summaryCheckpoint.test.js` (new): event shape, replay from checkpoint, two successive compactions chain the previous summary.

## Notes

ADR-M10. No change to `runLogEvents.js` members unless `model`/`tokensBefore`/`tokensAfter` are missing — then add them and update the snapshot once.

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M22)

A compaction checkpoint and `/compact` clear the chat's `memoryAsOf` so the rebuilt prefix includes the entries added since. Add a test (only if ADR-M22 is confirmed).

title: [Memory P3] beforeCompaction seam and memory flush before turns are dropped
body:
## Context

OpenClaw's pre-compaction flush (README §7 Phase 3): when a summary is about to drop turns, the Phase 2 extractor runs synchronously over exactly those turns, bounded to one call; failure never blocks compaction; summaries never become memory (Decision 10). `concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.6.

## Tasks

- [ ] `AgentLoop` seams: new hook `beforeCompaction(ctx, { dropping })` run before the summariser; a chat-turn seam registers `memoryExtractor.flushSync({ user, chatId, runId, turns: dropping, timeoutMs: 20000 })` when extraction is enabled for the turn's scope; without Phase 2 the seam is a no-op.
- [ ] The flush reserves a budget slot like any extraction, applies operations with the same snapshot checks, and records activity.
- [ ] A test that no summary text ever lands in `user-memory` except through the extractor's operations (seed a summary containing a unique token; assert the token is absent from every entry unless an operation carried it).

## Acceptance criteria

- Given extraction enabled and a compaction about to drop turns, then the extractor runs once over those turns before they are dropped; given it throws or times out, compaction proceeds; given extraction disabled, no flush.
- Given a fact stated in turn 3 and dropped at turn 150, then it is a memory entry (if durable) or in the summary (if episodic).

## Tests

- `tests/integration/memory-compaction.test.js` (new): flush-before-drop once; failure never blocks; summary stored on `summaryRef`; the no-summary-in-memory assertion.

## Notes

ADR-M10. Degrades to "no flush" without Phase 2 (product-plan §5.1).

body:
## Context

title: [Memory P4] memoryConsolidator: eligibility, inputs, prompt, parsing, guards, proposal
body:
## Context

Dream narrowly (README §5 Decision 11, §6.3 Consolidation, §7 Phase 4): a read-only-input, new-version-output pass over free-text notes that emits operations, not replacement prose, guarded by `maxPriorEntryLossFraction` and provenance, stored as `proposal { baseVersion, … }` and never applied in place (`concepts/2026-11-06 Agent Memory Research and Plan/architecture.md` §5.7, §6.5 prompt and tag parsing, §2.4 proposal shape; ADR-M11).

## Tasks

- [ ] New `server/services/memory/memoryConsolidator.js`: `isEligible(doc, settings)` (`version > consolidation.lastAppliedVersion`, `runsSinceLast ≥ minRunsSinceLast`, no proposal; `force` skips the run count); `collectInputs` (current notes, last `maxRunsRead` answers through `runHistory.js`, owner follow-ups as `memoryComposer.js:146-162`); the plain-text-tag prompt of §6.5 with numbered bullets; `llmClient.complete({ model: consolidation.modelId || run model, telemetry: { kind: 'utility', purpose: 'memory-consolidation', user: owner (null for profiles), surface: 'memory', redaction: { messages: 'hash-only' } } })`; parse `<notes>`, `<lessons>`, `<operations>` tolerantly (`parseComposerReply` style, `:238-252`); discard on `finishReason: 'length'`; compute `stats` and `lossFraction` by retained bullets; reject above `maxPriorEntryLossFraction`; drop lessons citing tool/fetched content (provenance); `setProposal(scope, proposal)` by CAS without touching `body`; `applyProposal(scope, { baseVersion, keepLessons })` under the lock → new version with `updatedBy: 'consolidation'`, lessons merged, proposal cleared, `consolidation.lastAppliedVersion` set, `409 MEMORY_PROPOSAL_STALE` when `version !== baseVersion`; `discardProposal`; `autoApply: 'notes-only'` applies notes and keeps lessons pending, recording the previous version for "Restore".

## Acceptance criteria

- Given an eligible task, then a proposal is stored with `baseVersion`, a diff, operations, notes, lessons and stats, and `body` is untouched; given a proposal that would lose more than 25 % of prior bullets, it is rejected and logged; given candidates from untrusted provenance, they are dropped; given a stale base, apply answers `MEMORY_PROPOSAL_STALE`; given `notes-only`, lessons are never auto-applied.
- The proposal keeps every `(seen YYYY-MM-DD)` watermark and is shorter than the input notes in the acceptance test.

## Tests

- `server/tests/memory/memoryConsolidator.test.js` (new) with fakes: eligibility; never mutates body; loss guard; provenance drop; stale apply; auto-apply notes-only; parsing tolerance; `length` discard.

## Notes

Code `MEMORY_PROPOSAL_STALE`, not `MEMORY_VERSION_CONFLICT` (C3).

## Amendment 2026-11-11 (ADR-M25)

The consolidator shows numbered bullets, parses `<operations>`, `<lessons>` and `<notes>` as in `architecture.md` §6.5, and runs `validateConsolidationPlan` before storing a proposal: references exist, no number twice, `maxOperations`, the newest `(seen …)` bullet is not dropped, the notes are the input minus the operations plus the merge results, unexplained loss rejects the plan, `maxPriorEntryLossFraction` applies to explained loss. Input over `maxInputChars` is `skipped: input_too_large` with no model call. The proposal stores the applied operations. Done when: the tests of `architecture.md` §10.8 pass.
